description:
## Why
One scroll tick lays out every window. c11 re-arms a full-window layout flush on every AppKit window update, and upstream measured 254 to 512 ms hangs on that path. Backlog item: B056.

## Evidence
origin/main `0ff8887e5e`, verified.

- `Sources/Workspace.swift:10138` observes `NSWindow.didUpdateNotification`.
- `flushWorkspaceWindowLayouts` at `:10238` lays out every `NSApp` window. The follow-up stays armed for about two seconds, and each update can schedule another flush.
- Upstream cmux #6801 (`8850142b8e`) removes that observer and keeps bounded stall retries and backoff. Deleting the observer alone strands repairs.
- Ride-along B067, probable: the follow-up calls `displayIfNeeded` on every window before the current display pass finishes (`Workspace.swift` near 10569 and the flush). Re-find. Upstream #2305 defers it.
- Research: Fable cluster C5. Memory of this workspace matches the observer. No c11 timing was measured. The upstream numbers are the evidence. C11-197, C11-202, and C11-205 are the hang records.

## Scope
In: scrolling does not schedule a layout of every window. Structural changes still converge: a split, a workspace switch, and a resize settle without a stuck divider. Port the bounded retry and the backoff reset with the observer removal.

Ride-along: B067. The follow-up must not call `displayIfNeeded` on every window from inside a display pass. Defer that flush to the next turn. If the probable trigger is gone on this SHA, say so and skip the code.

Out:
- Browser portal `layoutSubtreeIfNeeded` / `displayIfNeeded`. C11-287 owns that (ledger B014).
- Terminal portal `bind` doing the same inside a SwiftUI turn (B049). Tier-2 sweep.
- Sidebar bodies (B059).
- The mount cap (B012).
- Parked B038 (initial split ratios). Re-check only if a ratio is lost while you are in this flush. Do not expand.

## Approach
Remove the window-update observer. Keep a bounded retry that is armed by structural events (split, workspace change, resize), with backoff, as upstream did. Do not replace it with a timer that flushes all windows forever. Do not add a display link.

## Acceptance criteria
1. Scrolling a terminal in one window does not call the all-window flush on each scroll tick. A counter or a signpost in a debug build is enough, removed or compiled out before merge if it is not already behind `#if DEBUG`.
2. After a split and after a workspace switch, dividers sit where they were dropped, and a terminal is not stuck at the placeholder size. Retry is bounded. It stops.
3. Typing in the focused terminal during a scroll in another pane still lands. No new multi-hundred-millisecond main stall on the scroll path in a local sample.

## Validation
Tagged build on Atlas after C11-216. Computer use: scroll, split, switch workspace, and confirm the layout settled. A logic test only if the retry policy is a pure type. The C11-270 soak covers the hang budget. Do not claim the upstream 254 ms number as a c11 measurement. No source-grep test. No Hyperion build.

## Dependencies
None inside ws:bugs. Measure against a post-bump build if the Ghostty ticket has landed. Do not block on it. Cross-workstream: F1 is C11-216, F2 is C11-270. The lead links those.

## Risks
Deleting the observer without the retry leaves a split that never settles. That is the bug upstream hit. Deadlock-lite: `displayIfNeeded` inside an in-progress display pass. Defer it. Typing latency: this path is main-thread layout. Do not add work. Doctrine: no tenant config. No new strings. `dlog` stays inside `#if DEBUG`.

Size: S. Tier: P1. Doctrine check: layout follow-up only.
title: Stop scroll updates from laying out every window
